notes.claim: Lead acid uses constant-current constant-voltage charging: a regulated current raises the terminal voltage to the upper limit, then the current drops as the cell saturates.
The charge voltage limit is critical and ranges from 2.30 V to 2.45 V per cell.
Too low a limit risks sulphation on the negative plate; over-saturation by not switching to float causes grid corrosion on the positive plate.
The recommended float voltage of most flooded lead acid batteries is 2.25 V to 2.27 V per cell, and large stationary batteries typically float at 2.25 V per cell at 25 degrees C.
Charge voltage is reduced by 3 mV per cell for every degree above 25 degrees C and raised by 3 mV per cell for every degree below.
An equalising charge raises the voltage to 2.50 V per cell, about 10 per cent above the recommended charge voltage, to bring cells to similar levels.
Prolonged overcharge contributes to grid corrosion.
With CCCV, lead acid is charged in three stages: constant-current (bulk), topping (a falling current that saturates the cell) and float (making up self-discharge).
Full charge is reached when the topping current falls to 3 to 5 per cent of the Ah rating.
EnerSys's vented stationary cells float at 2.23 V per cell at 20 degrees C, and the charger voltage is the float voltage per cell times the number of cells.
EnerSys allows a boost recharge at 2.33 to 2.40 V per cell with the current limited to 4 x I10, and boost must be switched back to float once the battery is fully charged.
Charging beyond the specified limits turns the surplus energy into heat and the battery begins to gas.
EnerSys calls 2.40 V per cell the gassing voltage, and recommends a current limit of 2.5 to 5 A per 100 Ah above it.
In a string all cells receive the same charge current, so individual cell voltages cannot be controlled one by one.
Sulphation occurs when a lead-acid battery is deprived of a full charge.
An equalising charge is a deliberate overcharge to remove sulphate crystals that build up on the plates over time.
EnerSys corrects its vented cells' float voltage for temperature only outside its 10 to 30 degrees C range, by 0.003 V per cell per degree beyond 30, so makers' temperature rules differ.
Sealed (valve-regulated) cells are less tolerant of overcharge than flooded cells.
EnerSys says to recharge 1.2 times the discharged capacity, so about 83 per cent of the ampere-hours put in come back (lesson i4, charge efficiency).

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: The lead acid battery uses the constant current constant voltage (CCCV) charge method. A regulated current raises the terminal voltage until the upper charge voltage limit is reached, at which point the current drops due to saturation.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: The correct setting of the charge voltage limit is critical and ranges from 2.30V to 2.45V per cell.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: On one hand, the battery wants to be fully charged to get maximum capacity and avoid sulfation on the negative plate; on the other hand, over-saturation by not switching to float charge causes grid corrosion on the positive plate.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: the charge voltage should be reduced by 3mV per cell for every degree above 25°C and increased by 3mV per cell for every degree below 25°C.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: The recommended float voltage of most flooded lead acid batteries is 2.25V to 2.27V/cell. Large stationary batteries at 25°C (77°F) typically float at 2.25V/cell.

sources.title: BU-404: What is Equalizing Charge? - Battery University
sources.quote: Applying a periodic equalizing charge brings all cells to similar levels by increasing the voltage to 2.50V/cell, or 10 percent higher than the recommended charge voltage.

sources.title: Flooded Stationary Lead Acid Batteries IOM — EnerSys
sources.quote: After reaching the gassing voltage of 2.40 V/c a current limit of 2.5 to 5 A/100 Ah is recommended

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
sources.quote: Connected in a string, all cells receive the same charge current and controlling individual cell voltages as each reaches full capacity is almost impossible.

sources.quote: To reduce the recharge time the battery may be recharged at 2.33 – 2.40 V/cell with a current limited to 4 x I10. Boost charging must be switched to float charging when the fully charged state is reached.

sources.title: Bu 403 Charging Lead Acid — Battery University
